description: Canonical mathematical formulations for MAPEOGEO Wave F5

formulations.name: Banach Space Completeness
hypotheses: X is a normed vector space over R (or C)
Every Cauchy sequence in X converges to a limit in X
formulations.conclusion: X is a complete normed space (Banach space)

formulations.name: Hilbert Space Inner Product Completeness
hypotheses: H is an inner product space
H is complete with respect to the induced norm ||x|| = sqrt(<x, x>)
formulations.conclusion: H is a Hilbert space

formulations.name: Hahn-Banach Extension Theorem
hypotheses: X is a real normed vector space
M is a linear subspace of X
f is a bounded linear functional on M
formulations.conclusion: There exists a bounded linear functional F on X such that F|M = f and ||F|| = ||f||

formulations.name: Banach-Steinhaus Uniform Boundedness Principle
hypotheses: X is a Banach space
Y is a normed space
F is a family of bounded linear operators from X to Y
sup_{T in F} ||T x|| < infinity for each x in X
formulations.conclusion: sup_{T in F} ||T|| < infinity

formulations.name: Open Mapping Theorem
hypotheses: X and Y are Banach spaces
T: X -> Y is a bounded linear operator
T is surjective
formulations.conclusion: T is an open mapping (maps open sets in X to open sets in Y)

formulations.name: Banach Contraction Mapping Theorem
hypotheses: (M, d) is a nonempty complete metric space
T: M -> M is a contraction with Lipschitz constant q < 1
formulations.conclusion: There exists a unique fixed point x* in M with T(x*) = x*, and for any x0 in M, T^n(x0) converges to x* with geometric error bounds

formulations.name: Hilbert Space Adjoint Operator Existence and Pairing
hypotheses: H is a Hilbert space
T: H -> H is a bounded linear operator
formulations.conclusion: There exists a unique bounded linear operator T*: H -> H satisfying <Tx, y> = <x, T*y> for all x, y in H

formulations.name: Hilbert Projection Theorem and Orthogonal Decomposition
hypotheses: H is a Hilbert space
M is a closed convex subset (or closed subspace) of H
formulations.conclusion: For every x in H, there exists a unique y in M minimizing ||x - y||; if M is a subspace, H = M direct_sum M_perp and P is orthogonal

formulations.name: Neumann Series Inversion Theorem in Banach Algebras
hypotheses: A is a unital Banach algebra
x in A with ||x|| < 1

formulations.name: Spectral Theorem for Compact Self-Adjoint Operators
hypotheses: H is a Hilbert space
T: H -> H is a compact self-adjoint operator
formulations.conclusion: There exists an orthonormal basis of H consisting of eigenvectors of T, with real eigenvalues converging to 0, A = sum lambda_i P_i

formulations.name: Regular Sturm-Liouville Operator Resolvent Compactness and Expansion
hypotheses: L u = -(p u')' + q u on [a,b] with separated self-adjoint boundary conditions
p > 0, p in C1, q in C0, weight w > 0
formulations.conclusion: The Green operator G is compact self-adjoint on L2([a,b], w), yielding a complete orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions with real discrete eigenvalues lambda_n -> infinity

formulations.name: Picard Integral Operator Self-Map and Contraction Condition
hypotheses: y' = f(t,y) with |f(t,y)| <= M and |f(t,y1) - f(t,y2)| <= L |y1 - y2| on cylinder [t0, t0+h] x B_r(y0)
h <= r/M and h < 1/L
formulations.conclusion: The Picard operator (T y)(t) = y0 + int_{t0}^t f(s, y(s)) ds maps B_r(y0) into B_r(y0) and is a strict contraction with factor q = h L < 1

formulations.name: Picard-Lindelöf Local Existence and Uniqueness Theorem
hypotheses: U is an open subset of R x R^n
f: U -> R^n is continuous and locally Lipschitz in y
(t0, y0) in U
formulations.conclusion: There exists h > 0 such that the IVP y' = f(t,y), y(t0) = y0 has a unique C1 solution on [t0-h, t0+h]

formulations.name: Peano Existence and Non-Lipschitz Nonuniqueness Boundary
hypotheses: f: U -> R^n is continuous on open subset U of R x R^n
formulations.conclusion: There exists at least one local solution (Peano theorem); uniqueness may fail when f is not Lipschitz (e.g. y' = 2 sqrt(|y|))

formulations.name: Grönwall Integral and Differential Inequality
hypotheses: u, alpha, beta are continuous nonnegative functions on [t0, t1]
u(t) <= alpha(t) + int_{t0}^t beta(s) u(s) ds for all t in [t0, t1]
formulations.conclusion: u(t) <= alpha(t) + int_{t0}^t alpha(s) beta(s) exp(int_s^t beta(r) dr) ds for all t in [t0, t1]

formulations.name: Continuous and Lipschitz Dependence on Initial Data
hypotheses: y1, y2 are solutions of y' = f(t,y) with Lipschitz constant L on domain D
formulations.conclusion: ||y1(t) - y2(t)|| <= exp(L |t - t0|) ||x1 - x2|| for all t in existence interval

formulations.name: Maximal Solution Interval and Compactness Escape Boundary
hypotheses: f: U -> R^n is locally Lipschitz on open set U
y: (alpha, beta) -> R^n is a maximal solution of y' = f(t,y)
formulations.conclusion: As t -> beta- (or t -> alpha+), (t, y(t)) escapes every compact subset of U (either norm blows up or trajectory approaches boundary of U)

formulations.name: Autonomous ODE Local Flow and Group Action Law
hypotheses: x' = f(x) is an autonomous C1 system with local flow Phi_t(x)
formulations.conclusion: Phi_0(x) = x and Phi_s(Phi_t(x)) = Phi_{s+t}(x) whenever both sides are defined on connected maximal interval

formulations.name: Nonautonomous Linear System Two-Time Evolution Operator
hypotheses: y' = A(t) y is a linear nonautonomous system with continuous matrix A(t)
formulations.conclusion: The evolution operator U(t,s) satisfies U(t,s) U(s,r) = U(t,r), U(t,t) = I, and d/dt U(t,s) = A(t) U(t,s)

formulations.name: Regular Second-Order Two-Point Boundary Value Problem and Green Function
hypotheses: -u'' = f(x) on [0,1] with Dirichlet boundary conditions u(0) = 0, u(1) = 0
formulations.conclusion: There exists a unique C2 solution given by u(x) = int_0^1 G(x, s) f(s) ds where G is the symmetric continuous Green kernel

formulations.name: Transient Energy Growth in Nonnormal Stable Linear Systems
hypotheses: x' = A x with all eigenvalues having negative real part (Re(lambda_i) < 0)
A is nonnormal (A A^T != A^T A)
formulations.conclusion: The Euclidean norm ||exp(t A)||_2 may strictly exceed 1 for intermediate times t > 0 before decaying asymptotically to 0 as t -> infinity

formulations.name: Linearization and Indirect Lyapunov Method for Hyperbolic Equilibria
hypotheses: x' = f(x) with f(0) = 0 and Jacobian A = Df(0)
All eigenvalues of A have strictly negative real parts
formulations.conclusion: The origin is locally asymptotically stable for the nonlinear system; if any eigenvalue has Re(lambda) > 0, it is unstable

formulations.name: Lyapunov Direct Method and Orbital Derivative Criterion
hypotheses: x' = f(x) has an equilibrium at x = 0 (f(0) = 0)
V is a C1 positive-definite function on a neighborhood U of 0
V'(x) = grad(V)(x) . f(x) <= 0 on U
formulations.conclusion: The equilibrium x = 0 is Lyapunov stable; if V'(x) < 0 for x != 0, it is locally asymptotically stable

formulations.name: Conservative Hamiltonian Systems and Energy Invariant Foliations
hypotheses: q' = dH/dp, p' = -dH/dq for a C2 Hamiltonian function H(q, p)
formulations.conclusion: The Hamiltonian energy H(q(t), p(t)) is constant along all trajectories; phase flow preserves symplectic area and cannot have asymptotically stable equilibria

formulations.name: Validated Residual-to-Solution Error Bounds and Continuous Tubes
hypotheses: y-hat is a C1 approximate solution of y' = f(t,y) with residual r(t) = y-hat'(t) - f(t, y-hat(t)) satisfying ||r(t)|| <= R on [t0, t1]
||y(t0) - y-hat(t0)|| <= e0 and f has Lipschitz constant L on tube neighborhood
formulations.conclusion: The exact solution y(t) exists and satisfies ||y(t) - y-hat(t)|| <= exp(L(t - t0)) e0 + R (exp(L(t - t0)) - 1) / L for all t in [t0, t1]

formulations.name: Validated Positively Invariant Region and Trajectory Tube Enclosure
hypotheses: K is a compact box [a1, b1] x ... x [an, bn]
Vector field f points inward or tangent at all boundary faces of K
formulations.conclusion: K is positively invariant under the flow of x' = f(x): any trajectory starting in K remains in K for all t >= 0

formulations.name: Transversal Event Crossing and Root Isolation Certificate
hypotheses: Event hypersurface Sigma = {x : H(x) = 0}
Lie derivative L_f H(x) = grad(H)(x) . f(x) != 0 on enclosure box enclosing crossing
formulations.conclusion: The trajectory x(t) crosses Sigma transversely at a unique isolated event time t* within the validated time enclosure
